title: Speculative Knowledge Distillation: Bridging the Teacher-Student Gap Through Interleaved Sampling

contributions.purpose: Overcome the limitations of supervised KD (train-inference distribution mismatch) and on-policy KD (low-quality student samples that are OOD for the teacher, yielding inaccurate feedback) when distilling large LLMs into small students.
contributions.mechanism: Speculative Knowledge Distillation (SKD): interleaved sampling where the student proposes on-policy tokens and the teacher rejects/re-samples any token not in the teacher's top-K distribution (inspired by speculative decoding and imitation learning). Acceptance criterion is top-K membership; K=25 fixed, gamma=5 in practice. SKD dynamically degenerates to supervised KD early in training and on-policy KD later.
contributions.evaluation: Distilling Gemma-7B to Gemma-2B, SKD gains over supervised FT: low-resource translation +41.8%, summarization +230%, arithmetic reasoning +160%. Task-agnostic instruction-following: held-out MATH +198%, GSM-plus +360%. Tasks: Flores-200 Assamese-to-English (COMET), DialogSum (ROUGE-L), GSM8K (accuracy), UltraInteract math. Models: Gemma and Qwen families.
contributions.domain: LLM knowledge distillation / model compression for text generation
contributions.source_quote: A novel KD approach that utilizes on-policy student samples likely to be generated by the teacher, mitigating the issues of low-quality samples in on-policy KD and dynamically switching between supervised and on-policy KD.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate that SKD is broadly effective across diverse generation tasks and deployment scenarios rather than a single narrow setting.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical evaluation across summarization, translation, and reasoning tasks in both task-specific and task-agnostic distillation settings.
contributions.evaluation: SKD consistently outperforms existing KD methods (supervised KD, on-policy KD, ImitKD) across the tested text generation tasks in both task-specific and task-agnostic scenarios.
contributions.domain: LLM knowledge distillation for text generation
contributions.source_quote: Superior performance across various text generation tasks, including summarization, translation, and reasoning tasks, in both task-specific and task-agnostic scenarios.

contributions.purpose: Show SKD's practical reliability under varied training conditions, addressing on-policy KD's known sensitivity to student initialization.
contributions.mechanism: Systematic evaluation varying model initialization strategies, training data sizes (100/1K/10K), and model families (Gemma, Qwen); includes low-data regime and two-stage training ablation.
contributions.evaluation: SKD shows robustness and adaptability across different model initializations, data sizes, and model families; on-policy KD by contrast is highly sensitive to student initialization.
contributions.domain: LLM knowledge distillation for text generation
contributions.source_quote: Robustness and adaptability across different model initialization, data sizes, and model families.

self_declared_provenance.quote: SKD addresses above limitations by using major components from speculative sampling (Leviathan et al., 2023): 1) student model proposes on-policy sample candidate, and 2) the teacher model evaluates these proposed samples concurrently and accepts only those that it deems likely to generate.

The design of SKD is supported by theoretical results in imitation learning (Ross & Bagnell, 2010; Ross et al., 2011), which suggest that gradually shifting the sample generation from the teacher to the student is an effective approach.

we draw inspiration from top-k sampling (Radford et al., 2019) that draws samples using only the k highest probability tokens from the entire vocabulary V at each generation step. Following this intuition, we define our acceptance criteria based whether the student token falls into the top K tokens of teacher's distribution.

notes: Strongly positive framing throughout; large relative gains reported (percentages are relative improvement over SFT baseline). Baselines compared: supervised FT, supervised KD, on-policy KD, ImitKD. SeqKD was dropped because SFT consistently outperformed it. Note the reported gains are relative percentages off potentially low baselines (e.g. +360% on GSM-plus), so absolute magnitudes should be read from tables. No explicit negative result for SKD, but the paper highlights on-policy KD's sensitivity to initialization as motivation.
